surfaces.part: header cap of the sign (light lid with a blue slot)
blue sign board face with the white Korean text

answer.evidence: The sign is a tall, narrow board. Rows 1-5 form a light cap band 13 px wide, narrower than the 15 px body, with rounded upper corners. A darker line at row 5 (#738a90) works as the front-edge line, and the dark row 6 acts as eave shadow. The blue board face sits below it (rows 7-29, with the white text) and ends in a base strip at rows 30-31, giving about 25 rows of front face. The call is borderline: the cap could instead be read as a face-on header panel, since it has a blue label strip at row 3. The edge line plus shadow beneath it favours a top surface. No receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tall, narrow vertical sign in blue-grey with white 편의 lettering. It reads as a clean standing prop at the same scale as the references. Measured facts: 9 visible tones per tile, above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no large flat fills. 0% of dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outline is tinted dark blue rather than black. Shading is the weak point: the body has about 4 steps (highlight edge, mid, dark, deep outline), fewer than the 5-6 on the richer references. The sign face is mostly a flat blue panel with the lettering and little grain or speckle, and the tone count is carried by the text and edge. Next to vending-a and kiosk-a it looks a little simpler and thinner, though it is a plain signboard and not weaker than bus-shelter-a. A careful artist would likely accept it as a simple sign, but it sits at the low end of the standard, and the instruction is to fail when in doubt.

surfaces.part: top cap of the sign board
blue front panel with Korean lettering

answer.evidence: Rows 1-5 form a light cap band that widens from 13 to 15 px. It carries a blue slot at row 3 and ends in a darker front-edge line at row 5 (#738a90). Row 6 is a dark outline/shadow row (L=17), and the tall blue front panel (rows 7-29, 23 rows) sits below it. A base strip follows at rows 30-31. This is a top band with an edge line and shadow above a clear front face, so the sign reads as three-quarter view. The cap is short and the evidence is borderline, since the band could also be read as a front-facing header. No receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a slim vertical sign with a pale body, a dark navy-tinted edge, a lighter side highlight and shaded panel edges, plus the Korean text 편의 in a darker blue. The edge pixels lean blue, not neutral: the measured near-neutral share of dark edge pixels is 0%, the same as all three references, so the outline reads as dark_material_tone and not the sticker look. Near-flat coverage is 0%, lower than bus-shelter-a (9%) and equal to kiosk-a and vending-a, so there are no flat fills. At 9 visible tones per tile it is above bus-shelter-a (6) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). That is slightly lower than the richest reference, but it is a thin, single-surface sign, and the density is acceptable for that kind. It uses about 4 shading steps against roughly 5 in the references. A careful artist would accept it next to the shipped modern_city props without it looking noticeably flatter or more sticker-like.

surfaces.part: top cap of the sign (light band with a blue slot)
blue sign panel with lettering (vertical front face)

answer.evidence: This is a tall standing sign. The light cap at rows 1-5 widens from 11 to 13 to 15 px, so it reads as a bevelled top surface. At column x=11 rows 1-4 are all light (#f1f3f3), and a darker edge line at row 5 (#738a90) is followed by a dark outline at row 6 (#091125) acting as the eave shadow. The cap's blue slot is partly a face-on detail, so the cap is ambiguous, but the edge line and shadow count as evidence (a). Below it the blue lettered panel (rows 7-29) and the base (rows 30-31) form a front face of about 25 rows. The panel is a vertical face with no top of its own, but the cap covers it. No isometric side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tall vertical signboard with white Korean characters on a blue-navy body. Measured facts: 9 visible tones per tile, against 6 (bus-shelter), 12 (kiosk) and 20 (vending), so it sits within the reference range and above the bus shelter. Near-flat coverage is 0%, and 0% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is tinted dark blue, i.e. a dark material tone and not a black sticker line. The body shows about 4 shading steps: a light edge highlight, a mid blue, a dark side and a deep outline. Letters and a lit panel edge add variation, so there are no flat fills. It is a simple sign and has less texture than the vending machine, but it matches the kiosk and bus-shelter level and would sit acceptably next to them. Density is slightly lower than the richest reference, which is acceptable for a thin sign.

This reads as a horizontal top surface seen from above. Below it, the dark-blue board face (rows 7-29) with the Korean text and a grey base at row 30 gives a front face of about 24 rows. No receding side face is drawn. The cap is only 5 rows tall, but it has an edge line and shadow, so it is more than a rim.

That is above bus-shelter-a (6 tones) and below kiosk-a (12) and vending-a (20). The sign's flat panel areas are broken up by the lettering and a bevelled edge, and the measured flat coverage is 0%.
